subject: Data Structures
text: An array stores elements in contiguous memory locations and supports constant time access by index. Inserting in the middle may require shifting later elements.

subject: Data Structures
text: A linked list stores data in nodes connected by pointers. Inserting after a known node is efficient, but finding an item requires traversal from the head.

subject: Data Structures
text: A stack follows last in first out order. Push adds an item to the top and pop removes the most recently added item.

subject: Data Structures
text: A queue follows first in first out order. Enqueue adds at the rear while dequeue removes the item from the front.

subject: Data Structures
text: A binary search tree keeps smaller keys in the left subtree and larger keys in the right subtree. Its search cost depends on the height of the tree.

subject: Data Structures
text: A balanced AVL tree rotates after insertion or deletion to keep subtree heights close. This keeps search and update operations logarithmic.

subject: Data Structures
text: A heap is a complete tree that maintains a parent child priority rule. A priority queue can use a heap to remove the highest priority item.

subject: Data Structures
text: Depth first search explores one branch before backtracking. It can be implemented with recursion or an explicit stack.

subject: Data Structures
text: Breadth first search visits vertices level by level using a queue. In an unweighted graph it finds a path with the fewest edges.

subject: Data Structures
text: Merge sort divides an array into halves, sorts each half, and merges the results. Its running time is O of n log n.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: A relational database organizes information in tables made of rows and columns. A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: A foreign key references a key in another table and enforces referential integrity. It helps prevent records from referring to missing rows.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: Database normalization separates related facts into tables to reduce duplication. First normal form requires atomic values in each field.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: A SQL SELECT query retrieves rows from a table. WHERE filters records and ORDER BY sorts the returned result.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: An inner join combines rows when the join condition matches in both tables. A left join keeps every row from the left table.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: A transaction groups database operations into one unit. Atomicity and consistency help ensure a transaction either succeeds completely or has no effect.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: Two phase locking first acquires locks and then releases them. The protocol is used to control concurrent transactions.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: A B tree index keeps keys in sorted order across balanced nodes. The index can reduce disk reads when searching database records.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: A database view is a named query that presents selected rows or columns. Views can simplify access without duplicating the underlying data.

subject: Database Management Systems
text: An entity relationship diagram represents entities, attributes, and relationships. Cardinality describes how many records may participate in a relationship.

subject: Operating Systems
text: A process is a program in execution with its own address space and resources. The operating system creates and schedules processes.

subject: Operating Systems
text: Threads within the same process share memory and open files. Each thread has its own execution stack and program counter.

subject: Operating Systems
text: A CPU scheduler chooses which ready process runs next. Round robin scheduling gives each process a fixed time quantum.

subject: Operating Systems
text: Virtual memory gives processes a larger address space than physical RAM. Pages are moved between memory and disk as needed.

subject: Operating Systems
text: A page fault occurs when a process references a page that is not currently in physical memory. The operating system loads the page before continuing.

subject: Operating Systems
text: A deadlock can occur when processes wait forever for resources held by one another. Mutual exclusion and circular wait are among its required conditions.

subject: Operating Systems
text: A mutex provides exclusive access to a shared resource. A thread locks the mutex before modifying shared data and unlocks it afterwards.

subject: Operating Systems
text: The file system stores files and directories on persistent storage. Permissions determine which users can read, write, or execute a file.

subject: Operating Systems
text: System calls let an application request services from the operating system kernel. Opening a file and creating a process are common examples.

subject: Operating Systems
text: A context switch saves the state of one running process and restores another. Switching too often adds scheduling overhead.

subject: Computer Networks
text: The Internet Protocol routes packets between networks using source and destination IP addresses. Routers examine network layer headers.

subject: Computer Networks
text: The Transmission Control Protocol establishes a connection and retransmits lost data. Sequence numbers help deliver an ordered byte stream.

subject: Computer Networks
text: The User Datagram Protocol sends datagrams without connection setup or guaranteed delivery. Applications can use it when low latency matters.

subject: Computer Networks
text: The Domain Name System translates a human readable hostname into an IP address. A resolver can cache DNS answers for later requests.

subject: Computer Networks
text: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol defines request and response messages between a client and a web server. HTTPS protects HTTP with TLS.

subject: Computer Networks
text: A router forwards packets between different IP networks. A switch forwards frames within a local area network using MAC addresses.

subject: Computer Networks
text: A subnet mask separates the network portion of an IPv4 address from the host portion. Subnetting divides a network into smaller address ranges.

subject: Computer Networks
text: Ethernet defines framing and media access for wired local area networks. A switch learns source MAC addresses to build its forwarding table.

subject: Computer Networks
text: Transport layer ports identify the application endpoint for network traffic. A server listens on a port for incoming client connections.

subject: Computer Networks
text: A firewall applies rules to allow or block network traffic. Rules can consider addresses, ports, protocols, and connection state.

subject: Machine Learning
text: Supervised learning fits a model from examples paired with known target labels. The fitted model predicts labels for new input features.

subject: Machine Learning
text: A training set is used to fit model parameters while a separate test set estimates performance on unseen examples. The test data must not influence feature fitting.

subject: Machine Learning
text: A decision tree splits examples using feature conditions. Limiting its depth can reduce overfitting on a small training set.

subject: Machine Learning
text: A support vector machine chooses a separating boundary with a large margin between classes. A linear SVM is useful with sparse text features.

subject: Machine Learning
text: Precision measures the fraction of predicted positive examples that are correct. Recall measures the fraction of actual positive examples that are found.

subject: Machine Learning
text: TF IDF gives more weight to terms that are frequent in one document and uncommon across the collection. It represents text as numeric feature vectors.

subject: Machine Learning
text: Cross validation trains and evaluates a model across multiple folds of the training data. The held out test set remains untouched for final evaluation.

subject: Machine Learning
text: A confusion matrix counts actual labels against predicted labels. It shows which categories a classifier tends to confuse.

subject: Machine Learning
text: Overfitting occurs when a model fits details of its training examples but performs poorly on new data. More representative data and regularization can help.

subject: Machine Learning
text: A classification model predicts a discrete category such as a document subject. Evaluation should include class aware metrics when classes are imbalanced.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: A search agent explores possible states to find a path from an initial state to a goal. Breadth first search expands the shallowest unexplored states.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: A heuristic estimates the remaining cost from a state to a goal. A star search combines path cost so far with the heuristic estimate.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: A knowledge based system stores facts and rules about a domain. An inference engine applies the rules to derive additional conclusions.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: A constraint satisfaction problem assigns values to variables while satisfying constraints. Backtracking search can undo assignments when a conflict appears.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: A minimax agent selects a move by considering alternating choices from itself and an opponent. The search tree represents possible game outcomes.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: Alpha beta pruning skips game tree branches that cannot change the minimax decision. It can search deeper without changing the selected move.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: A Bayesian network represents random variables and conditional dependencies as a directed acyclic graph. Conditional probability tables quantify the relationships.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: A planning system represents actions with preconditions and effects. A plan is an ordered set of actions that reaches a desired goal state.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: An intelligent agent observes its environment and chooses actions to achieve goals. A rational action is evaluated using the agent's performance measure.

subject: Artificial Intelligence
text: Natural language processing enables computers to work with human language. Tokenization divides a sentence into words or other meaningful units.
